newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Australia denies rebuffing Cambodia asylum-seekers.
newsitem.headline: Australia denies rebuffing Cambodia asylum-seekers.

text.p: Australia's ambassador in Phnom Penh on Monday denied that his embassy had refused asylum to frightened opponents of co-premier Hun Sen in the aftermath of the violent ouster of his coalition partner.

Foreign sources, speaking on condition they were not identified, said on Sunday that some embassies had refused asylum to supporters of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, despite several political killings.
The sources said that the U.S. and Australian embassies were among the missions which had been refusing to protect fearful supporters of Ranariddh.
"It's not true," ambassador Tony Kevin told Reuters. "No one asked for asylum in our compound."
An official of the U.S. embassy said opponents of Hun Sen were not categorically being turned away.

The foreign sources said hundreds of soldiers and supporters of Cambodia's ousted premier have been detained and political killings and other abuses which occurred in the aftermath of Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of Ranariddh on July 6 were continuing.
The Sydney-based Sun-Herald newspaper on Sunday quoted a leaked diplomatic cable from Kevin to his government, saying Canberra should support Hun Sen.

Describing Hun Sen as a democrat at heart, the cable said supporting Ranariddh would only prolong the fighting in Cambodia, the paper said. A government official in Canberra said the government could not comment on leaked cables and Kevin also declined to comment on Monday.

The foreign sources said at least three high-ranking FUNCINPEC officials had been executed, including Secretary of State for Interior Ho Sok, intelligence officer Chao Sambath and Undersecretary of State for Defence Krouch Yoeum.
Government officials said Ho Sok was executed by enraged soldiers loyal to Hun Sen after being arrested last Monday.

The foreign sources said they feared for the safety of FUNCINPEC soldiers at three main detention sites in the vicinity of the capital. They were picked up by patrols during and after two days of fighting in Phnom Penh on July 5 and 6.
Several hundred soldiers were being kept at one of the sites and detainees at another site were receiving no food, they said.
The sources said there were reports of Ranariddh's supporters in the provinces being arrested, detained and beaten for allegedly possessing illegal weapons.
Hun Sen has said his rival's soldiers will be released.

On Friday, the London-based human rights organisation Amnesty International expressed "grave fears" for the safety of hundreds of soldiers and officials of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party in the custody of Hun Sen's forces.
